text:
Alex Chen: FYI seeing sustained p95/p99 regression for the hosted generate endpoint since ~09:10 UTC. Grafana alert fired and we have 4 customer escalations about high tail latencies. p95 jumped from ~180ms to ~520ms, p99 up to ~1.8s.
Maria Patel: Oof. Any model/region skew?
Alex Chen: Mostly rw-v4-large in us-west-2, but there are a few spikes in eu-west-1 too. Traffic pattern shows a big prefix-heavy workload (very long prompt prefixes) starting ~09:05.
Oncall Bot: ALERT: High tail latency — channel=eng-sre, severity=high, alert_id=ALRT-2145.
Chen Li: I can start triage. First checks: model replica CPU/GPU util, queue length, batch size distribution, and KV cache hit rate. Priya, can you take support escalations?
Priya Singh: On it. Replied to customers asking for repro steps/ETA. Notifying customers we'll fallback to smaller model if needed.
Alex Chen: Repro steps I used:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-v4-large","input":"<2000-token prefix> + short instruction","max_tokens":512}'
```
You can see p99 locally hitting ~1.6s for that exact request. Also observed increased KV cache miss rate: cache_hit_rate dropped from 92% -> 54% at the same time.
Chen Li: Metrics I pulled: PromQL snippets below for reference.
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model))
sum(rate(requests_in_queue[1m])) by (model, region)
sum(rate(kv_cache_misses_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total[5m]))
```
Chen Li: GPU util on affected pools is ~65% (not saturated). However queue length for rw-v4-large in us-west-2 spiked to ~1200 concurrent requests and avg batch window widened (we're waiting longer to create batches). That explains higher per-request latency.
Maria Patel: So root cause appears to be increased concurrency + poor cache locality causing batching to blow up latency.
Alex Chen: Agreed. Proposed mitigations (short list):
- Immediate (minutes): enable emergency circuit breaker on /v1/generate for rw-v4-large in us-west-2 to cap concurrency and shed load. Add a conservative rate limit at the gateway for non-SLA tenants. Enable automatic fallback to rw-v4-small for requests that exceed threshold.
- Short-term (1–3 hours): roll out additional rw-v4-large replicas (scale up), temporarily enable smaller max_batch_size and reduce batching window to reduce tail waits, increase KV cache TTL for common prefixes, pin hot customer traffic to dedicated pool if possible.
- Medium (1–2 days): tune batching heuristics (workload-aware batching), add model routing rule based on request size to prefer smaller models for prefix-heavy requests, improve prefix/KV caching strategy (prefix fingerprinting).
- Postmortem actions: add p95/p99 SLO dashboards per-model-region, implement automatic circuit-breaker config tied to queue depth and request_duration SLO.
Priya Singh: For immediate steps I can: update customer comms (ETA 1 hour), enable fallback on the gateway and throttle non-paid tiers. Anything else I should say to customers?
Support Lead: Tell them we're actively mitigating, fallback to a smaller model might slightly change output but should preserve correctness. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline.
Chen Li: Technical playbook details for on-call (copy/paste):
1) Run `kubectl get pods -l app=inference,model=rw-v4-large -o wide` to find pods with high restart counts or OOMs.
2) Check queue depth: `curl -s http://orchestrator.internal/metrics | jq '.queues["rw-v4-large"].depth'`
3) Flip circuit breaker: POST to orchestrator `/v1/admin/circuit-breakers` body `{\"model\":\"rw-v4-large\",\"region\":\"us-west-2\",\"max_concurrency\":200}`
4) Apply gateway rate limit: `redis-cli set ratelimit:gw:non-sla 50` and push config.
5) Enable fallback routing: `orchestrator apply-routing --from=rw-v4-large --to=rw-v4-small --when=queue>400`

Chen Li: Note: when flipping circuit breaker, we should also set a short cooldown and monitor error rates — we don't want cascading 429s without fallback.
Alex Chen: Also enable region fallback policy for critical customers: route to eu-west-1 rw-v4-small if us-west-2 queue > 600 and latency > 800ms.
Maria Patel: For SLO guardrails we should add automated actions:
- If p95 > 500ms OR queue_depth > 500 => reduce batching window by 50%, set per-tenant concurrency cap to 200.
- If p99 > 1.2s AND error_rate < 0.5% => enable fallback to smaller model.
- If error_rate > 1% => pause auto-fallback and escalate to engineers.
Priya Singh: Implementing fallback now. Rolling out a temporary gateway rule that maps rw-v4-large -> rw-v4-small for requests longer than 1500 tokens and for non-enterprise tenants.
Oncall Bot: ACTION: circuit-breaker applied for rw-v4-large/us-west-2 by Chen Li at 09:24 UTC.
Alex Chen: After circuit breaker live: queue depth down from 1200 -> 220 over ~6 minutes; p95 improved from 520ms -> 240ms, p99 down to ~820ms. We're still above baseline but much better.
Maria Patel: Great. Next steps: keep the breaker for 30 minutes while scaling replicas and tuning batching. Please capture metrics and open a postmortem ticket. Assign to infra and runtime teams.
Support Lead: I'll update all customers that we applied mitigations and ETA for full fix is 48 hours. Will include expected change in output when fallback used.
Chen Li: I'll create follow-up tasks: batching tuning RFC, prefix caching improvement, and automated SLO guardrails.
Alex Chen: Thanks everyone. I'll monitor dashboards and we'll reconvene in 30m.
Priya Singh: Customers notified, one confirmed their traffic dropped and latency improved.
Maria Patel: Filing postmortem template: `https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/RI-POST/` + link will be added once created.
Alex Chen: Closing thread for now — keep updates in this thread if anything regresses. :thumbsup:
